answer:
As far as I know, LlamaIndex's `TokenTextSplitter` has no `separator_regex` parameter, so it has no default for one.

It takes a plain-string `separator`, which defaults to `" "` (a single space). It also has `backup_separators`, which defaults to `["\n"]`. The other main parameters are `chunk_size` (default 1024) and `chunk_overlap` (default 20).

You may be thinking of `SentenceSplitter`, which has a regex-based `secondary_chunking_regex`. Its default is `"[^,.;。？！]+[,.;。？！]?|[,.;。？！]"`. Other libraries, such as LangChain's text splitters, use similar regex-based separator options.

I haven't checked this against the source for your installed version. If you need to be certain, check the class signature with `help(TokenTextSplitter)`.
